messages.author: 1fe638ac9008754d
messages.subject: Potential date of upcoming changes to language
parts:
Hello,

I am giving some lectures here (at Oxford) on Bayesian statistics this term. For the applied problems I set for the class, I want to use Stan. I am currently about to start writing the lectures on the Stan language. Before I do so, I wanted to check first - do you know when the somewhat major changes to the language might be made? For example, on the developers' email list I have received some messages about replacing ~ with @ etc.

Do you know yet what these changes might be? Finally, do you know if there will be back-compatibility? 

I was hoping to make the students aware of these changes, and also potentially reduce the number of changes to the lectures I make between this year and next!

Apologies if this is already decided, and I have missed it. However, wanted to check.

Best,

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Pontential data of upcoming changes to language
parts:
Thanks for bringing this up --- it's a very legitimate concern
that I keep bringing up myself.

Here's a complete list of the planned changes:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/wiki/Stan-3-Density-Notation-and-Increments

Each plan change is clearly (I hope) laid out and distinguished
from the background discussion. 2.10 will have at least these changes:

* = replacing <- for assignment

* target += ... replacing increment_log_prob(...)

In both cases, the existing behavior is deprecated, so there'll be
full backward compatiblity. I'm in the middle of adding the vertical
bar and _lpdf, etc. notation, but it probably won't make it until
2.11.

We're not going to break backward compatibility until we
release Stan 3, and that's probably at least a year out
at the pace we're going. We hope to do that with automatic
translation scripts for models, but no promises (we're very
shorthanded for core Stan development below the interfaces
level). And even with Stan 3, we might still support our
old syntax and not remove it until Stan 4. I'm terribly worried
about running into a Python 2.x vs. 3.x problem. We can't
afford to fork our entire community because the core dev team
is too small.

- Bob

Thanks Bob. Really really helpful.

 For what it's worth (not a lot, I suspect) I would really favour backwards compatibility for Stan 3. Having seen what has happened with Python, I wouldn't want it to go that way for Stan! In fact one reason I prefer Stan over the multitude of arising platforms is its stability of language.

Best,

Ben
